title: Machine-learning screening and experiments identify two new superconductors, Be₂HfNb₂ and Be₂Hf₂Nb
summary: An AI-accelerated workflow screened more than 1.3 million material structures, combining a graph-neural-network model of superconducting properties with density-functional calculations and stability filters. The researchers experimentally synthesized and confirmed superconductivity in Be₂HfNb₂ and Be₂Hf₂Nb, reporting two previously unreported compounds among 741 computationally screened stable candidates. The two compounds were confirmed in the Be₂Nb₃ substitution series; other listed candidates remain computational predictions.
ai_technology: BEE-NET equivariant graph neural networks in an AI-accelerated high-throughput screening workflow
organization: University of Florida; Oak Ridge National Laboratory; Quantum Formatics

evidence.tested: An AI-accelerated workflow screened more than 1.3 million material structures, combining a graph-neural-network model of superconducting properties with density-functional calculations and stability filters.
evidence.unknown: The AI model accelerated candidate selection but did not itself perform the synthesis; DFT and laboratory confirmation were essential. The paper reports an overall screening precision of 86%, so most candidate predictions were not experimentally verified in this study.
evidence.ai_role: Predicted Eliashberg spectral functions and superconducting transition temperatures to prioritize candidate structures, followed by DFT stability calculations and experimental synthesis/characterization by the research team.
